caveats: THIS POLYGON IS AN INDICATIVE CORRIDOR, NOT A SURVEYED DISPOSAL BOUNDARY. It is reconstructed from two OSPAR inventory points, the published 50 km x 3.5 km dimensions and the cited centre point. It must NOT be used to determine whether a location is safe to fish, dredge, anchor or lay cable.

Extent is deliberately coarse. The 1996 Aberdeen Marine Laboratory survey (FRS 1996) found munitions and munitions-related materials at high densities OUTSIDE the charted dumpsite, so the real distribution is wider than any published boundary can express.
The OSPAR inventory itself flags dumpsite locations as uncertain: 'one of the major difficulties in managing the risk associated with dumpsites is the uncertainty associated with their location'.
The UK MoD lost most disposal records, disclosed April 2020. Completeness is therefore unestablished rather than disproved.

Operation Buffalo and Hurricane were AUSTRALIAN nuclear weapons tests, not British, and not at this site. Beaufort's Dyke received ordnance and chemical-agent DUMPING. Do not attribute weapons testing here.
A 1996 survey found no chemical agent or munitions-derived contaminants adjacent to the dyke in sediment, fish or shellfish. That is reassuring, not exculpatory, given the record loss.

properties.name: Beaufort's Dyke
properties.reconstructedFrom: OSPAR inventory entries 16 and 19, extended to the published 50 km length and widened to the published 3.5 km width.
properties.munitionsTonnage: over 1 million tonnes conventional and chemical munitions (MoD estimate, OSPAR); some sources cite up to 2 million tonnes including short-dumped material
properties.chemicalAgents: ca 14,500 t of 5-inch artillery rockets filled with phosgene dumped July 1945; a further ca 14,000 t of phosgene loose-dumped 1946-47
properties.radioactiveWaste: ca 2 tonnes of low-level radioactive waste in concrete-encased drums, authorised in the 1950s-60s
properties.dumpingClosed: Under the London and Oslo Conventions, 1972; last dumping ca 1976
properties.coordSource: Reconstructed corridor from two OSPAR dumpsite inventory coordinates plus published dimensions. Not a survey.
